notes.1a: Most candidates only scored one of the three available marks as their answers were not related to IAS 38.
notes.1b: This was well answered although only a few candidates scored full marks. It is essential for International Accounting Standards (IAS) terminology and correct labelling to be used.
notes.1c: Many candidates calculated the working capital cycle correctly but a significant number used the quoted credit terms of 30 days rather than calculating the turnover days from the given information.
notes.1d: Most candidates made a reasonable attempt and did provide appropriate improvements actions. Some candidates did not state whether or not liquidity could be improved.
notes.2a: Only a few candidates demonstrated an understanding of the role of the internal auditor.
notes.2b: Performance was varied with some excellent responses but also some poor ones. Very few candidates provided an appropriate explanation for information 3 but there were some good responses for the other three items with good application of the relevant IAS.
notes.2c: Many candidates made the inventory adjustment correctly but relatively few adjusted correctly for the depreciation.
notes.2d: Few candidates produced a correct statement of changes in equity. Many omitted the paid dividend and some did not account for the profit for the year.
notes.2e: The statement of financial position was produced to a high standard with many scoring full marks. Those candidates who had made errors in previous parts of the question were rewarded for transferring their own figures to the statement.
notes.2f: Few candidates performed well on this part.
notes.3a: This was very well answered with any candidates scoring full marks.
notes.3b: This was also well answered with many candidates scoring full marks. A few candidates incorrectly referred to the profit as a surplus and a limited number either omitted the purchases adjustments or made errors in its calculation.
notes.3c: This was generally well answered. Some candidates made errors with labels and balances.
notes.3d: Many candidates provided the four required actions and scored full marks.
notes.3e: This was not answered so well with few candidates able to state relevant advantages and disadvantages.
notes.4a: The consignment account was prepared to a high standard with few errors. The most common error was not posting the final amount to the income statement.
notes.4b: Candidates did not do well on preparation of the account. Most candidates used incorrect labelling in the account.
notes.4c: Candidates did not prepare the goods sent on consignment account well. Most candidates used incorrect labelling.
notes.4d: The preparation of this account was reasonable with most providing some correct entries. A limited number of candidates did reverse the entries.
notes.4e: This was well answered with most candidates able to provide two valid answers.
notes.4f: Most candidates did make a decision but the reasoning was often not valid. Some stated that the home project was ‘high risk’ despite the question clearly stating that there was a guaranteed return of 12%.
notes.5a: Most candidates answered this part well.
notes.5b: Most candidates calculated the material and labour variances correctly but were unable to calculate the fixed overhead variances.
notes.5c: The reconciliation was prepared to a reasonable standard with most candidates transferring their own calculated variances to the statement correctly. Many candidates struggled with the standard production cost although most dealt correctly with the actual production cost.
notes.5d: Most candidates did provide a decision. The justification was generally acceptable with most gaining two or three extra marks and a limited number obtaining full marks.
notes.6a: Most candidates demonstrated an understanding of net present value but only a limited number appeared to understand the internal rate of return with many believing that it did not use the time value of money.
notes.6b: This was very well answered with many candidates scoring full marks. Those that did make some errors in the calculation of the cashflows generally still scored high marks as they applied the discounting process correctly to their own figures.
notes.6c: This was also well answered with some candidates scoring full marks. Some candidates did make some calculation errors but none were common and overall performance was satisfactory.
notes.6d: Most candidates did provide a reasonable analysis of the benefits.
notes.general_comments:
Overall candidates performed reasonably well. The numerical parts of questions were answered better than
the written parts.
